recognize_zh: 胸水抹片中一大群黏著的上皮樣細胞旁，有兩顆胞質塞滿紫紅色異染性顆粒（metachromatic granules）的肥大細胞，另散在小淋巴球。
features: Large cohesive three-dimensional cluster of epithelioid cells with round eccentric nuclei and vacuolated blue cytoplasm
Two mast cells at the cluster edges with cytoplasm packed with purple-red metachromatic granules and a round nucleus
Additional granular cell within the cluster
Scattered small lymphocytes around the cluster
describe_en: Cytocentrifuge preparation of pleural fluid shows a large cohesive cluster of epithelioid cells with round eccentric nuclei and vacuolated basophilic cytoplasm. Two mast cells with cytoplasm filled with coarse purple metachromatic granules lie at the edges of the cluster, and small lymphocytes are scattered nearby. The epithelioid cluster cannot be definitively classified as reactive mesothelial cells versus metastatic carcinoma on morphology alone. Findings show mast cells in pleural fluid accompanying a cohesive epithelioid cell cluster; immunocytochemistry (calretinin, WT1, claudin-4, MOC-31) is recommended for the cluster.

ddx.vs: Basophils are smaller with a lobulated nucleus and fewer, larger, water-soluble granules, whereas mast cells have a round nucleus with densely packed granules.

ddx.dx: Reactive mesothelial cells vs metastatic adenocarcinoma
ddx.vs: Mesothelial cells show windows and knobby borders and are calretinin/WT1-positive, while adenocarcinoma forms three-dimensional balls with claudin-4/MOC-31 positivity.
Siderophages have golden-brown to blue-black refractile pigment and a bean-shaped nucleus rather than uniform purple metachromatic granules.
